scope: Oath first-printing multiplayer core: Law October 20, 2020; corresponding full Playbook; official base errata November 15, 2022; Card/Site Reference; no bots or expansions.
verdict: CHALLENGE: two distinct core rules remain untested explicitly; do not yet accept working saturation.

findings.source: Law 7.5.4, printed p9; Card Reference p1 Common Icons; Longbows illustrations in Playbook pp6,18,24.
findings.finding: No question or full expected answer tests the meaning of the dual-sign battle-plan icon: its user may choose to add or remove the shown die type. Existing questions test role colors, fixed additions/removals and an empty attack-pool reduction, but not this source-defined choice.
findings.why_distinct: The sign is an operational permission with two different dice-pool outcomes, not cosmetic card artwork or a new numeric example. The role color restricts who may use the plan; it does not select its sign.
findings.ledger_challenge: The broad Law7.5 and Card Reference mappings do not establish coverage of 7.5.4. Passes9/10 can remain historical zero-addition passes, but this independent finding resets the stopping rule once accepted.

findings.source: Law7.3.1 and7.3.4, printed p9; Law7.1.3, printed p9; Law4.1.4, printed p5.
findings.finding: Q029 asks frequency of Wake/Rest powers and states optional Rest, but does not explicitly ask whether an inconvenient ordinary Wake power can be skipped. Its answer says Wake once each in Wake without explicitly explaining the required-versus-optional boundary. The People’s Favor requirement and Opportunity exception are separately covered, but not this generic Wake rule.
findings.why_distinct: A generic standalone Wake effect happens once at its timing; ordinary choice to skip a Rest power does not make Wake effects optional. This is an explicit source-defined permission boundary, not another frequency or named-card example.
findings.ledger_challenge: The generic standalone-power map currently treats frequency coverage as covering mandatory-versus-optional use. Add the explicit branch rather than crediting a repeated once-per-phase question.

proposed_additions.question: A battle plan you rule has a gradient power box and a ± attack-die symbol. Must an attacker add the die and a defender remove it, or may either user choose either sign? Does ± also let you change defense dice?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: Either the attacker or defender may use a gradient battle plan and choose to add or remove the attack die shown. The plus/minus symbol means add or remove the type of die shown; it does not switch an attack-die effect into a defense-die effect, and the user’s role does not choose the sign. Normal battle-plan access, payment and once-per-Campaign rules still apply.
material_facts: The user chooses add or remove; attacker/defender role does not determine the sign.
The effect applies to the die type shown; ± attack die does not also authorize changing defense dice.
Gradient permits either side, subject to the ordinary battle-plan rules.
source_references: Law 7.5.4 Iconography, printed p9: battle plans with a +/– symbol can add or remove the type of die shown.
Law 7.5 introductory paragraph, printed p9: gradient boxes allow attacker or defender.
Law 7.5.1–3, printed p9: rule/access, use timing, payment and use limit.
Card Reference p1 Common Icons: Add or remove symbol.
proposed_additions.novelty_credit: One distinct rule: dual-sign choice and its die-type scope. No separate novelty credit for repeated role/color, payment or once-per-Campaign facts.

proposed_additions.question: You have a faceup card effect beginning “Wake:” whose text contains no “may”. May you choose to skip it because it would be inconvenient, just as you can decline a “Rest:” power? Is taking Opportunity-site income at Wake compulsory too?
proposed_additions.expected_answer: No. Wake powers happen during your Wake Phase, once each; you do not have a general option to skip such a Wake effect. Resolve as much of its effect as possible, respecting its conditions and other restrictions, except any parts that explicitly say “may”. Rest powers are optional and may be used once each at the end of Rest. Taking one favor or secret at Salt Flats, Mine or Drowned City is explicitly optional, so you may decline that income.
material_facts: An ordinary Wake effect with no optional wording is not freely skippable; it happens once during Wake.
Resolve as much as possible subject to conditions/restrictions; explicitly may parts remain optional.
The explicit Opportunity-site income permission is optional.
source_references: Law7.3.1 Wake, printed p9: Wake powers happen once each during Wake; the reminder distinguishes mandatory powers from optional taking of site favor/secrets.
Law7.3.4 Rest and Law4.3.5, printed pp9,5: Rest powers may be used once each at end of Rest.
Law7.1.3 Use, printed p9: must resolve as much as possible except parts saying may.
Law4.1.4 Use Site Power, printed p5; Site Reference p2 Opportunity Sites: may take one favor or secret.
proposed_additions.novelty_credit: One distinct generic rule: mandatory ordinary Wake use versus optional Rest/explicit may. No additional novelty credit for repeated frequency or already-tested Opportunity income.

source_key_review.potential_wording_note: Q031 says enemy adviser in a question already framed around an enemy adviser. Its full answer first permits theft from a co-located player, as Law5.1.4.IV requires; do not infer an additional enemy-only theft restriction from the shorthand.

coverage_assessment.overall: The 93-question bank has broad substantive procedural coverage. Two explicit generic power rules remain untested directly: dual-sign battle-plan choice and required ordinary Wake effects versus optional Rest/explicit may. Working saturation should remain provisional.
coverage_assessment.first_and_later_setup: Covered separately by Q021–Q025/Q083–Q085; first game does not inherit later-game bottom draws/random preparation.
coverage_assessment.all_four_oaths_and_visions: Covered by Q001–Q005/Q036/Q073–Q075/Q088; no new Oath/asset recombinations count as additions.
coverage_assessment.campaign_both_winners: Attacker victory and optional/mandatory consequences covered by Q014–Q017/Q077; defeated attacker covered by Q038; Q093 explicitly covers victorious defender, defeated effects and either-side end-discard. New A01 concerns generic sign choice rather than another outcome-cleanup example.
coverage_assessment.chronicle: All ordered steps and the specified errata covered by Q020/Q045–Q052/Q075/Q085, including Archive shortage, ruin preservation/order, Dispossessed eligibility and relic refill-before-stack.
coverage_assessment.sites: All Site Reference power families represented by Q053–Q064/Q092; travel overrides, local pawn versus rule access, capacity and suit-specific Homeland suppression checked.
coverage_assessment.powers_and_technical_glossary: All major operational families represented, but broad maps miss direct testing of Law7.5.4 sign semantics and Law7.3.1 required-versus-optional Wake use. Generic Move/Swap/Play, Draw correction, Give/Take distinction, private info and hierarchy are represented.
coverage_assessment.historical_question_handling: All ten remain retained without deletion or renumbering and receive zero novelty credit in this review.
